independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The actual source fixes ||Cu0||=2 yet defines residual 1-||Cu||^2/2, which equals -1 at the stated target, and its lower Jacobian omits the second C. On an admissible transport principal eigenline, the written update is a_next=(1-mu/2)*a+1/(mu*a), giving an error1/2 from the exact target amplitude even as only the starting eigenvalue error tends to zero. This contradicts (3.59). Positive fission scaling preserves H1-H6, so the eigenline is not an arbitrary matrix substitution. Normalization-only correction has derivative 1-mu and can repel for mu>2; only the explicitly stated scalar true-Newton repair is certified.

The source's purported negative gradient has the wrong sign in the scalar-residual term; its imposed f-perpendicular projection conflicts with the equation <f,w>=s. The admissible mu=lambda=1 eigenline test has the prescribed zero start, a strictly ascending written direction and a projected stationary point; every projected update has Q>=s^2/2 when s!=0. Choosing amplitude near the corrected normalization shows an independent failure of arbitrary-accuracy update realization.

The contour is centered at mu_bar and necessarily encloses the scalar pole in addition to the nearby eigenvalue. On the principal eigenline the residues sum to -mu_bar, whereas the claimed inverse action is mu_bar*mu/(mu_bar-mu). Clockwise orientation changes only the integral sign and does not restore equality. The counterexample can satisfy the gap-dependent closeness assumptions; convergent quadrature of the stated contour computes the wrong operator.

severity_correction.reason: Theorem 5.1 is explicitly a main result of the global initialization strategy. Its admitted transport initial data can make the first normalization undefined. The later nonnegative-data lemma repairs a restricted domain but does not validate the stated central guarantee.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: For D=(0,1), V=[-3/2,-1] union [1,3/2], sigma>0 constant, kappa=0 and positive constant fission, H1-H6 hold and F=c*P_v. The principal eigenfunction is not velocity-constant, so h=(I-P_v)u1 is nonzero with positive right overlap after normalization, but C h=0. The first power normalization is undefined under the actual stated condition. The source calls this global initialization guarantee a main result; its failure is central and warrants Major rather than the prior Minor grade. Lemma5.6 explicitly positive data and the properly oriented nonzero Riesz-component result remain restricted counterevidence.

assumptions_checked.details: H1 requires bounded convex D with piecewise C1 boundary. H2 excludes zero velocity, normalizes velocity measure and adopts all-direction sphere/energy coordinates. H3 supplies nonnegative L2 kernels and bounded row/column integrals. H4 gives bounded sigma and positive absorption-minus-scattering margin alpha. H5 gives a uniform positive fission lower bound. H6 is printed as phi in C(closure(D); L2(D x V)); this notation is retained without silently replacing it by a different hypothesis.

assumptions_checked.locator: PDF p.16 / printed p.704, Theorem 2.6; PDF pp.53-55 / printed pp.741-743
assumptions_checked.details: The Newton countercheck uses the paper's simple positive principal eigenpair, and hence its own intended admissible setting. It does not require an arbitrary matrix to be realizable as a transport operator. The countercheck is on the real subspace with the paper's weighted Hilbert norm.
Actual page image confirms norm(C u_degree)=2, not sqrt(2). The same value is repeated in the actual image of printed p.712, equation (3.32) and the LBB normalization argument.

locators: H3-H4 on PDF p.9 / printed p.697
Theorem 2.5 and Lemma 2.4 on PDF p.14 / printed p.702
Appendix A on PDF p.52 / printed p.740
checked_results.method: Direct weighted energy and Schur/Cauchy-Schwarz calculation
reasoning: Let S=ess sup sigma and rho=1-alpha/S. H4 implies both scattering row and column integrals are bounded by sigma-alpha <= rho sigma. Thus 0<=rho<1.
For u=T^{-1}K g with homogeneous inflow, integration by parts gives integral u(v.grad u)=(1/2) integral_{Gamma+} u^2 v.n >=0. Consequently ||u||_sigma^2 <= integral kappa u g.
Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz and the two row/column bounds give integral kappa |u g| <= rho ||u||_sigma ||g||_sigma, so ||T^{-1}K||<=rho<1.
The characteristic formula for T^{-1} preserves nonnegativity. Therefore B^{-1}=(I-T^{-1}K)^{-1}T^{-1}=sum_{j>=0}(T^{-1}K)^j T^{-1} is positive. F is positive, hence C=B^{-1}F is positive.

The same symmetric splitting of the scattering quadratic form gives Re(Bu,u)>=alpha ||u||_L2^2 for homogeneous inflow. It yields the stated L2 inverse bound when the source operator is defined on the established domain.
The weighted norm equivalence follows directly from alpha<=sigma<=S, with square-root constants. The check does not rely on the precise numerical factors printed in (2.24).
checked_results.limitations: This verifies the displayed energy/positivity mechanism. The full ultraweak trace and Babuska-Necas theorems cited from prior literature were not independently reproved.

locators: Appendix B, PDF pp.53-55 / printed pp.741-743
checked_results.method: Check of the operator factorization and the consequences of the stated positive-kernel property
reasoning: The correct factorization is C=(I-T^{-1}K)^{-1}T^{-1}F. Since the first factor is bounded by the Neumann argument, compactness follows if T^{-1}F is compact.

Taking adjoints reduces this last property to compactness of F^*T^{-*}; the paper invokes an external compact-embedding result for F^* on the transport graph space. The logical reduction is valid; the cited external embedding is not claimed as newly verified.

On the all-direction velocity domain adopted in H2, convexity of D and the uniform fission lower bound explain why the composition F T^{-1} F connects positive-measure source sets to interior phase-space points. The appendix explicitly relies on the resulting strictly positive kernel.

Given this positivity property, C^2 maps nonzero nonnegative functions to strictly positive functions. If a real eigenvector w at the principal eigenvalue changed sign, both C^2(|w|+w) and C^2(|w|-w) would be strictly positive, giving C^2|w|>|C^2w|. Pairing with a positive adjoint principal eigenvector contradicts equality of the two spectral pairings. This supports geometric simplicity.

Algebraic simplicity then also follows from the adjoint eigenvector: if (C-mu I)w=u were a Jordan-chain equation, pairing with the positive adjoint eigenvector u_star would give 0=<u,u_star>, impossible for positive u and u_star.
checked_results.limitations: The compactness premise is reference-dependent in the source. No independent claim is made for an alternative velocity-domain interpretation or a silently corrected H6 function-space notation.

locators: Lemma 3.1, equations (3.20)-(3.22), PDF pp.21-22 / printed pp.709-710
checked_results.method: Independent Fredholm argument using algebraic simplicity
reasoning: Let e be a unit right principal eigenvector, C e=mu e, and P the orthogonal projection to e-perp. The compression Q=P(I-C/mu)|_{e-perp} is identity minus a compact operator.
If Qw=0 for w in e-perp, then (I-C/mu)w=c e. Pairing with the adjoint principal eigenvector gives c=0 because its pairing with e is nonzero. Thus w is in span(e) and e-perp, so w=0.
Fredholm index zero now gives surjectivity and a bounded inverse. Hence theta=1/||Q^{-1}||>0, as claimed.
This argument does not require an invariant orthogonal complement, normality of C, or a complete generalized-eigenvector expansion for the whole compact operator.
checked_results.limitations: The quantitative relation between theta and the spectral gap in Remark 3.2 was not certified by this check.

locators: Theorem 3.3 and equations (3.30)-(3.33), PDF pp.23-24 / printed pp.711-712
checked_results.method: Direct block decomposition at a principal eigenvector
reasoning: For u=a e with a>0, the printed block A(u,lambda)=[I-lambda C,-C u; -<C u,.>,0] has lower row -mu a<e,.>.

At lambda=1/mu, the lower row determines the component of the solution along e. The compressed-resolvent inverse determines the orthogonal component; the remaining e-component of the first row determines the scalar unknown. Thus this printed block is boundedly invertible at the principal eigenpair.

Continuity of A then supplies some invertible neighborhood. This positive fact does not identify A as the derivative of the displayed residual, and therefore does not establish the claimed Newton error estimate.

A consistent residual with its actual derivative has a locally invertible augmented eigenpair Jacobian under algebraic simplicity and a normalization functional nonzero on the principal eigenvector. The paper's explicit constants and tolerance analysis require rechecking after such a repair.
checked_results.limitations: The explicit beta/tau constants and the universally quantified bilinear inequalities in Lemma 3.8 were not certified. The universal inequality as printed cannot hold for z'=-z; a correct inf-sup formulation is a possible local repair, not an additional Major finding here.

findings.title: The residual, normalization and displayed Jacobian are inconsistent; the printed iteration violates Theorem 3.10
locators: PDF p.19 / printed p.707: explicit iterates (3.8)-(3.9)
PDF p.24 / printed p.712: repeated normalization in (3.32) and the LBB proof
PDF pp.31-32 / printed pp.719-720: Theorem 3.10, (3.59), and its use of R(u_degree,lambda_degree)=0
exact_source_claims: The target is normalized by ||C u_degree||=2.
The scalar residual is R2(u,nu)=1-||C u||^2/2.
The lower row in the displayed derivative and the defining update equation is -<C u,.>.
Theorem 3.10 asserts a quadratic bound around this normalized target for every sufficiently close initial guess.
findings.derivative_check: On the real Hilbert space, D R2(u,nu)[h,eta]=-<C u,C h>=-<C^* C u,h>. This differs from the displayed -<C u,h>. The check already fails on a real eigendirection, so complex-differentiability conventions cannot remove it.
findings.normalization_check: At the specified target, R2=1-2^2/2=-1. Therefore the proof's statement R(u_degree,lambda_degree)=0 is false.
hypotheses_and_quantifiers: Choose the paper's principal eigenpair C e=mu e with mu>0 and ||e||=1 in its stated weighted norm. Let u=a e and lambda_degree=1/mu.

The prescribed target is a_degree=2/mu. For any sufficiently small nonzero epsilon choose lambda=lambda_degree+epsilon; isolation of the principal eigenvalue allows this point to remain in the resolvent of M_lambda.

The initial pair (a_degree e,lambda_degree+epsilon) belongs to every specified positive-radius neighborhood for sufficiently small epsilon. It also respects the explicit formulas' condition lambda != lambda_degree.
No finite-dimensional matrix approximation or unsupported source-model realization is needed: the calculation restricts the paper's actual operator to its own invariant principal eigenspace.
analytic_calculation: On that eigenspace, z=M_lambda^{-1}C(a e)=[mu a/(1-lambda mu)]e.
Substitution into (3.7)-(3.8) gives a_next=(1-mu/2)a+1/(mu a), independently of lambda whenever 1-lambda mu is nonzero.
At the written target a=2/mu this is a_next=2/mu-1/2. Hence the eigenvector error after one step is exactly 1/2, while the initial combined error is |epsilon|.
For the finite constant K=beta_bar gamma/2 in (3.59), choosing epsilon sufficiently small yields 1/2>K epsilon^2. Thus the stated quadratic estimate fails even with invertible M_lambda.
At lambda=lambda_degree the block formulation (3.4) is also well-defined and gives the same nonzero step from the exact target, but the nonzero-epsilon argument avoids relying on this boundary case.
independent_normalization_repair_test: Merely changing the target normalization to ||C u||=sqrt(2) gives a_star=sqrt(2)/mu, a fixed point of the printed scalar iteration.
The derivative of that scalar iteration at a_star is 1-mu. It is generically nonzero, so the printed method is not locally quadratic even after that normalization change.

If mu>2, the fixed point is repelling on the eigenline. Such values are not excluded: replacing an admissible positive fission kernel by t times that kernel preserves H1-H6 with adjusted finite bounds and scales C and mu by t.

The correctly differentiated residual instead gives a_next=a/2+1/(mu^2 a), whose derivative at a_star is zero. This verifies the specific missing-factor mechanism on the eigenline, without certifying all corrected infinite-dimensional constants.

details.method: Exact rational arithmetic for the printed equations, not an RTE discretization or author-code run

counterevidence_considered: Actual images show the value 2 in (3.1), so it is not an OCR loss of a square root.

The value 2 is used repeatedly in the LBB argument, and the missing C is repeated in both the displayed derivative and the block update, so the inconsistency is not confined to a detached introductory formula.
The explicit formulas initially assume lambda != lambda_degree; the epsilon-offset calculation satisfies this condition.
Special scaling mu=1 could hide the first-order defect on one eigendirection after renormalization, but no hypothesis imposes mu=1 and the original normalization contradiction persists for every mu.
The operator positivity and compressed-resolvent results do not fix the residual/Jacobian mismatch.
findings.impact: This affects the central exact Newton theorem and any later perturbation/accuracy-control claim that invokes that exact theorem with the printed residual and updates. It does not by itself refute the radiative-transfer principal-eigenpair existence theory or a consistently reformulated Newton method.
findings.requested_correction: Use a residual and normalization that share the stated target, differentiate that residual correctly, and rederive the block inversion, Lipschitz bounds, convergence neighborhood, and dependent tolerances for the corrected scheme. Replacing a single normalization constant does not suffice.
findings.attribution: The parent and this native helper independently identified the normalization/Jacobian mismatch. The parent explicitly requested and also independently supplied the nonzero-epsilon strengthening. This helper verified the source images, derived the scalar calculation, and ran the retained exact-rational check.

definitions_and_dependencies.operator: C=B^{-1}F on the Hilbert trial space U. M_lambda=I-lambda C. The principal positive eigenpair satisfies C e=mu e and lambda=1/mu.
definitions_and_dependencies.implementation_quadratic: For fixed outer iterate, f=Cu, g=M_lambda u, s=1-||f||^2/2, and Q(w,nu)=1/2[||M_lambda w-nu f+g||^2+(s-<f,w>)^2].
definitions_and_dependencies.inner_accuracy: Equation (4.1) requires the computed update to be within an arbitrary prescribed eta in the full product-space norm.
definitions_and_dependencies.power_initialization: Section 5 starts with ||a0||=1 and <a0,u1>!=0. Lemma 5.6 later adds a0>=0 and writes E_C(mu1)a0=alpha u1 with alpha>0.

Conditional valid Newton estimates in this receipt require a consistent residual with a true zero and its actual derivative; they do not validate the printed inconsistent scheme.

findings.assessment_note: Supported independent failure of the proposed CC3 update realization.
findings.title: The printed descent direction and projected iteration do not solve the stated least-squares update problem
findings.location: Equations (4.28)-(4.31) and projected descent immediately below (4.31)
findings.claim: The paper calls D in (4.30) the negative gradient of Q and claims the projected scheme can realize any requested Newton-update accuracy.
findings.exact_derivative: Writing r=M_lambda w-nu f+g, the true gradient is (M_lambda^* r+(<f,w>-s)f, -<f,r>). Hence its negative has first component -M_lambda^*r-(<f,w>-s)f. Equation (4.30) instead prints a plus sign on this rank-one term.

counterexample.admissibility: Let e be any normalized principal eigenfunction. Multiplying the strictly positive fission kernel by a positive constant preserves H1-H6 and scales C, so choose the scale Ce=e. Set lambda=1, u=a e with a>0 and s=1-a^2/2!=0. The amplitude a can be arbitrarily close to the residual-compatible normalization sqrt(2), so the issue survives a normalization repair.
counterexample.reduction: Then f=a e, g=0 and, on w=t e, Q(t e,nu)=1/2[a^2 nu^2+(s-a t)^2]. Its unique eigenline minimizer is (t,nu)=(s/a,0). The exact second block requires <f,w>=s.
counterexample.strict_ascent: At (w,nu)=(0,0), the true gradient is (-a s e,0), while the printed D is also (-a s e,0). Therefore the directional derivative of Q along the printed D equals a^2 s^2>0. It is a strict ascent direction.
counterexample.projected_failure: The printed initialization w0=f-P_span(f)u is zero for Ce=e, and nu0=0. Projection of D1 onto f-perp annihilates -a s e, and D2=0. Every projected iterate therefore remains (0,0), with Q=s^2/2 and update error at least |s|/a.
counterexample.general_obstruction: Even after correcting the gradient sign, forcing w into f-perp leaves the second residual equal to s, so Q>=s^2/2 whenever s!=0. Such iterates cannot meet arbitrary eta; a quadratic outer tolerance of order error^2 cannot in general tolerate an error floor of first order.

repair_and_limits: Use the true negative gradient and the full product space for the consistent block system. If its matrix/operator A is boundedly invertible, Q has Hessian A^*A and ordinary Hilbert-space gradient descent with a suitable step converges.

If a subspace reduction is desired for the printed Q, the second block requires the affine constraint w=(s/||f||^2)f+v with v perpendicular to f, not w perpendicular to f. A repaired actual Jacobian may change that row and must be used consistently.

This finding is independent of the earlier residual/Jacobian mismatch: it already contradicts the paper's own explicitly displayed quadratic objective. Repairing the normalization alone does not fix it.
The correctly derived gradient on the preceding lines of PDF40 is counterevidence against a deliberate new optimization method; the final sign and the zero-offset projection still require correction.

findings.assessment_note: Supported failure of the alternate contour-based CC3 realization.
findings.title: The contour representation encloses a pole of its scalar factor and is not the asserted inverse operator
findings.claim: The contour Gamma is centred at mu_bar=lambda_bar^{-1}, encloses the principal eigenvalue mu, and is asserted to represent M_lambda_bar^{-1}C by integrating [mu_bar zeta/(mu_bar-zeta)](zeta I-C)^{-1}.

counterexample.reduction: Take an exact principal eigenvector e with Ce=mu e, mu>0, and choose mu_bar!=mu sufficiently close that the proposed disc encloses mu. It also necessarily encloses its centre mu_bar.
counterexample.actual_integral: For positive orientation the scalar integrand on this eigenline is mu_bar zeta/[(mu_bar-zeta)(zeta-mu)]. Its residues at mu and mu_bar are respectively mu_bar mu/(mu_bar-mu) and -mu_bar^2/(mu_bar-mu). Their sum is -mu_bar. Thus the displayed integral equals -mu_bar e.
counterexample.orientation_check: Clockwise orientation changes the result to +mu_bar e; neither orientation yields the asserted inverse for a general nearby mu_bar.
counterexample.explicit_values: For example mu=1 and mu_bar=101/100 give desired value 101 e but contour value -101/100 e (or +101/100 e with reverse orientation). Any positive spectral separation allows mu_bar to be chosen sufficiently close to satisfy the stated near-eigenvalue condition; the numerical choice is illustrative, not an asserted transport spectrum.
counterexample.impact: Increasing quadrature accuracy cannot make this incorrect contour integral converge to the claimed inverse action, even if every shifted resolvent is evaluated exactly.

repair_and_limits: Holomorphic functional calculus for this rational function requires a contour/domain enclosing the required spectrum while excluding the pole mu_bar, or a correct explicit separation of the principal spectral projection and the complementary inverse.
Such a repair must account for the amplification 1/(mu_bar-mu); it cannot be achieved by changing only the orientation.

The printed conversion following (4.35) also requires the right side zeta^{-1}B u: multiplying (zeta I-B^{-1}F)w=u by B gives (B-zeta^{-1}F)w=zeta^{-1}B u. This is recorded as an associated algebraic correction, not a separate finding.
The implementation is described as a proposed alternate route with details deferred. That limitation is respected, but its decisive analytic identity is already false.

findings.assessment_note: A local missing initial-data restriction; Lemma 5.6 supplies the intended nonnegative-start repair.
findings.title: Theorem 5.1 needs a nonzero principal Riesz component rather than only a nonzero inner product with the right eigenfunction
findings.location: Initialization before (5.1), Theorem 5.1, compared with Lemma 5.6
findings.claim: The stated initial condition is ||a0||=1 and <a0,u1>!=0, with no nonnegativity condition before Theorem 5.1.

transport_counterexample.model: Take d=1, D=(0,1), V=[-3/2,-1] union [1,3/2] with ordinary Lebesgue measure, sigma=sigma0>0 constant, kappa=0, and phi=c>0 constant. V has total mass one, is compact away from zero, and contains S^0={-1,1}. The other domain, boundedness, accretivity, strict-fission positivity and continuity assumptions H1-H6 hold.
transport_counterexample.velocity_projection: Let P_vel h(x,v)=integral_V h(x,v')dv'. Since |V|=1, P_vel is the orthogonal velocity-average projection in L2; constant sigma also preserves this orthogonality in the weighted variant. Here F=c P_vel and B=T.
transport_counterexample.nonconstant_velocity: A nonzero principal right eigenfunction u cannot be independent of v. Otherwise u(x,v)=h(x) and the transport equation reads v h'(x)+sigma0 h(x)=lambda c h(x) for almost all v. Taking two distinct velocities gives h'=0, and the homogeneous inflow trace forces the constant h to be zero, a contradiction. The equality is valid distributionally; bounded velocities away from zero give the required one-dimensional weak derivative.
transport_counterexample.initial_vector: Set b=(I-P_vel)u, which is nonzero, and a0=b/||b||. Then ||a0||=1 and <a0,u>=||b||>0 by orthogonality, so the written right-eigenvector condition holds.
transport_counterexample.failure: F a0=0, hence C a0=B^{-1}F a0=0. The first normalization in (5.1) is undefined. This uses an admissible transport model, not an arbitrary matrix substituted for C.

repair_and_counterevidence: The correct general spectral requirement is E_C(mu1)a0!=0. Its scalar coefficient depends on the left eigenfunction, not only on <a0,u1>. A phase/sign convention is also needed to converge to the chosen signed u1.
Lemma 5.6 explicitly assumes a0>=0 and correctly uses E_C(mu1)a0=alpha u1 with alpha>0. This excludes the sign-changing counterexample and supplies an accessible intended class.
Under the stated positivity/irreducibility assumptions, a nonzero nonnegative initial function has positive principal projection. The Riesz decomposition then gives the intended convergence.
Because the needed condition is explicitly present in the later lemma, this is classified as a local Minor scope correction, not a refutation of the intended nonnegative-start method.

checked_results.claim: Conditional inexact-Newton recurrence and stopping estimates
reasoning: For a consistent residual R with R(z*)=0, actual derivative J, uniform bound ||J(z)^{-1}||<=B and Lipschitz derivative constant L on the local neighborhood, direct Taylor integration gives ||z-J(z)^{-1}R(z)-z*||<=(B L/2)||z-z*||^2.
An update computed within eta_n therefore obeys e_{n+1}<=eta_n+(B L/2)e_n^2. Thus eta_n=O(e_n^2) preserves quadratic convergence; eta_n<=zeta e_n/2 and e_n<=zeta/(B L) give e_{n+1}<=zeta e_n.

This direct estimate avoids comparing the perturbed error to an independently evolving exact-iteration error. It is conditional on staying in the invertibility neighborhood and on repairing the core residual/Jacobian defect.

The triangle bounds (1-c e_n^{p-1})e_n<=||z_{n+1}-z_n||<=(1+c e_n^{p-1})e_n hold for the full pair z=(u,lambda). The printed equations (4.20)-(4.21) display only the u increment although e_n is a pair error; that component-only estimate is not certified here.

For an actually quadratic residual with its true derivative, the midpoint identity R(z)-R(z*)=J((z+z*)/2)(z-z*) is exact. A generic vector-valued mean-value assertion would not be enough, but this specific quadratic structure permits the corrected local residual equivalence.

With B as the bound on the actual inverse derivative, the lower residual coefficient is 1/B. This receipt does not certify the printed beta-bar reciprocal placement or the constants inherited from the inconsistent Section 3 formulas.

checked_results.claim: Error propagation for an approximate application of C=B^{-1}F
reasoning: If ||Ff-F_eta1 f||<=eta1 in the source norm and the approximate B inverse has error <=eta2, then triangle inequality yields ||C f-[B^{-1},[F,f;eta1];eta2]||<=||B^{-1}||eta1+eta2.
This verifies Remark 4.4's budget. The separate approximation routines and their correct norm-dependent bounds are prerequisites; this check is not an execution of them.
The source explicitly relies on the earlier source-solver work for B^{-1} and on wavelet compression/low-rank application methods for F. This helper did not retrieve or execute that external work.

checked_results.claim: Qualitative power convergence under the proper principal-projection condition
reasoning: Let E be the principal Riesz projection and Q=I-E. With E a0=alpha e, alpha!=0, and spectral radius of C|range(Q) strictly less than mu1, choose any delta with q=|mu2|/mu1<delta<1. The spectral radius formula, or a contour lying inside |z|<mu1 delta and surrounding the complementary spectrum, gives ||(C/mu1)^n Q||<=K_delta delta^n.

Consequently (C/mu1)^n a0=alpha e+O(delta^n). After normalization this converges to the phase/sign of alpha times e; for a nonnegative start the phase is positive. The paper's elementary unit-vector angle identity then transfers a line-distance estimate to the vector estimate.
For normalized a_n and e, |<Ca_n,a_n>-mu1|<=(||C||+mu1)||a_n-e||, confirming linear Rayleigh-quotient convergence under these conditions.
General nonnormal compactness does not by itself give a useful numerical bound for K_delta. The paper acknowledges this; no uniform dimension-free or spectrum-only resolvent norm claim is accepted.

The printed Neumann-series formula (5.11) contains factorial denominators, and (5.16) swaps gap and ratio in its final algebra. The underlying restriction identity follows directly from commutation of resolvents with the Riesz projection, and the correct contraction ratio is q+beta(1-q)=1-Delta+beta Delta.

The proof of (5.19) treats the singular value of mu1 E as mu1 although an oblique rank-one projection contributes ||E||. The ambient operator C E_Q also differs from the restriction C|range(Q). The latter, with the inherited Hilbert norm, has singular values bounded by those of C by orthogonal compression. This provides a possible local repair, but the exact printed Schatten constants and their complete propagation are not certified here.
No additional Major finding is inferred from these repairable/local proof issues without showing a separate failure of the corrected qualitative conclusion.

The abstract, introduction, Section 5.2 and conclusion explicitly state that knowledge of spectral-gap and related conditioning information remains an obstruction to a complete certified implementation.

Section 5 provides an idealized power iteration and says perturbed realization details are deferred. Section 4.4 similarly sketches implementations and leaves details and numerical work to future work.
Sections 4-6 contain analytical algorithms and implementation discussion, not a newly reported benchmark table or numerical experiment to reproduce. No empirical success or software run is inferred.
The heuristic monitoring of Rayleigh quotients is explicitly labelled heuristic; it is not treated here as a certified lower or upper spectral enclosure.
The supplied manifest records optional code/supplements as not_located_in_bounded_search. This is historical bounded-search evidence, not a claim of nonexistence and not a mathematical defect.
